messages:
kevin: Quick idea from spike today: instead of long-lived customer private endpoints or full VPC peering, what if we run a tiny 'control-plane sidecar' inside the customer VPC that only proxies control/config traffic to our global control plane? No user data, just control plane. Thoughts?

lina: Clarify: sidecar runs in customer account, accepts local agent connections, and opens an outbound mTLS session to cp.redwood.net? If so, that's interesting - reduces our need for cross-account routing.

samir: Upside: fewer peering/router changes and simpler infra on our side. Downside: many enterprise customers require stable egress IPs for allowlists. Outbound sidecar traffic will have customer's NAT IPs unless they provide static egress.

anya: Operationally, we trade a few regional relays for many tiny agents. Upgrade and rollback story becomes important: can we canary sidecar versions? auto-rollback? Also, licensing/compliance questions since code runs in customer accounts.

kevin: Proposed contract (draft): sidecar is intentionally stateless, connects to cp-prod.redwood.net:443 via mTLS, validates short-lived tokens, and proxies local calls. If controlplane unreachable, sidecar can optionally forward to a regional-relay (customer opt-in).

kevin: Example config (very rough):
```yaml
sidecar:
  listen: 127.0.0.1:15050
  controlplane: cp-prod.redwood.net:443
  auth: sts
  token_ttl: 300s
  egress_mode: none # none | managed-egress | peering
  fallback: regional-relay
```

lina: Security: avoid writing long-lived secrets to disk. Sidecar should fetch ephemeral credentials via an STS-style flow, optionally using a KMS/HSM attestation for stronger binding. Consider host attestation to prevent spoofing.

samir: For customers requiring fixed egress, offer: (A) managed egress appliance (we deploy a small NAT/EIP pair in their account), or (B) keep peering as a paid option. Keep both on catalog.

anya: Monitoring and logs: enterprise customers will ask where logs/metrics reside. Provide three modes: send to Redwood, forward to customer's ingest (e.g., Splunk/Datadog endpoint), or keep local for air-gapped needs. Document retention and redaction defaults.

kevin: Failure modes that popped up in spike: token refresh storms after network outage, rapid reconnects causing control-plane thrash, and split-path acceptance if both sidecar + relay are enabled simultaneously. Need jittering/backoff and circuit breakers.

lina: Compromise risk: if host is compromised, attacker could proxy malicious control messages. Mitigations: short TTLs, per-instance certs, attestation signatures, and restrict allowed control-plane verbs for sidecar-only mode.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: cp-sidecar-spike branch pushed to staging. CI link: https://ci.internal/6789 build green :white_check_mark:

samir: Perf notes from staging: p50 handshake ~22ms eu-west, p99 ~70ms under 2k simulated agents. Memory ~60MB per sidecar. Need 5k+ test for confidence and outage recovery tests.

lina: I'll draft a failure-mode document enumerating connectivity, token refresh, health-check, and compromise scenarios. Also propose a minimal network ACLs doc for customers.

anya: I'll draft a customer/network requirements one-pager for sales: clearly call out egress options (sidecar-only, sidecar+managed-egress, peering), firewall rules, and expected operational responsibilities.

kevin: I'll prototype a tiny PoC binary and a Helm chart for customers who want self-managed sidecar. Default remains opt-in. If this converges, we'll capture as RFC follow-up with migration/playbook and decision matrix.

lina: Agree. Also include a note in the sales doc: customers with strict outbound IP controls should be steered to managed-egress or peering.

kevin: Thanks everyone. Revisit in one week after failure-mode doc and scale tests. :thumbsup:
